question.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot {2}^{1-3x} & \ge {(\frac{1}{3})}^{x-4} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot {2}^{1-3x}) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x-4}] \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(1-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & \ge (x-4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(1-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & \ge (x-4)(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(1-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & \ge (x-4)(0-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(1-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & \ge (4-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+\operatorname{ln}⁡2-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & \ge 4\operatorname{ln}⁡3-x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & \ge 4\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & \ge 3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3\operatorname{ln}⁡2=\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡8.$ Since $3<8,$ we know that $\operatorname{ln}⁡3<\operatorname{ln}⁡8.$ Therefore, $\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡8<0.$ Because we are dividing both sides of the inequality by a negative number, we must reverse the direction of the inequality sign:

$$
x\le \frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}
$$
